Amplify the voices of young professionals, ensuring that the next generation plays a role in shaping space governance. And develop educational and advocacy programs to engage youth and policymakers on sustainability. This initiative aligns with global efforts to promote responsible space practices while integrating young professionals into decision-making processes. IPAS presents a structured set of recommendations that are focusing on key sustainability concerns in space governance. And the 3 core areas of policy focus have the baseline of establishing a clear framework for the intergenerational pact for space sustainability. The first one is space debris, with the recommendation of implementing binding rules on debris prevention, increasing investment in reusability, and advancing debris removal technologies. Then on space traffic management, there are recommendations on developing a global framework for data sharing and collision avoidance protocols. And finally, on space resources, defining foundational principles for intergenerational sustainability, ensuring equitable access and responsible use of space resources. The IPAS report also includes recommendations for enhancing youth participation. So to ensure that meaningful inclusion of the youth, IPAS called for a youth advisory board at UNOSA, similar to the the one existing at the ITU, incorporating youth delegates in all national COPUS delegations, and increased investment in youth-led initiatives including paid internship, educational programs on space sustainability, and scholarships and capacity-building events. These measures are all essential to ensuring a multi-generational approach to space policy and space sustainability. So on dark and quiet skies, why does it matter for our proposed intergenerational pact? Preserving dark and quiet skies is fundamental to the sustainability of astronomy, planetary science, and space exploration. Increasing numbers of satellites and megaconstellations pose a risk to both optical astronomy and radio astronomy, and effective regulatory measures must be in place to mitigate these impacts and ensure that scientific advancement and environmental preservation go hand in hand. So by integrating dark and quiet skies considerations into broader sustainability frameworks, we can create a balanced approach to outer space utilization where technological progress does not come at the cost of astronomical science. To advance the protection of dark and quiet skies, IPAS proposes 3 key areas of action. Advocacy and policy engagement. So we want to ensure youth representation in expert groups discussing dark and quiet skies, strengthen national and international regulations to limit light pollution, and radio frequency interference and integrate dark and quiet skies preservation measures into global space traffic management best practices. The second area is industry and scientific collaboration. So we want to promote research and innovation in dark and quiet skies-friendly technologies and sustainable satellite design and foster collaboration with scientific bodies to advocate for industry standards that minimize satellite impacts. And finally, on public awareness and education, we aim to utilize creative media and storytelling, for example, social media campaigns, infographics, short films, all to engage a broader audience and organize workshops and outreach programs to educate students, professionals, and the general public on the importance of dark and quiet skies. So by implementing these strategies, we want to bridge the gap between space sustainability and astronomical heritage, ensuring that future generations can continue to explore and understand the universe without interference. Our next steps are continuing engaging with international space bodies to promote intergenerational sustainability and space policy, strengthen collaboration with space agencies, industry leaders, academic institutions to support practical applications of dark and quiet skies preservation measures. And finally, expand the youth-led initiative and campaigns to raise awareness about dark and quiet skies, sustainability, and responsible space governance. By working together, we can ensure that the next generation is empowered to uphold the principles of responsible space stewardship.
